Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
The failing test `ClassUtilsTest.test_getPackageName_Class` is calling the `getPackageName` method from `ClassUtils` class with an argument of type `String[].class`. 

The current issue report states that `ClassUtils.getShortClassName()` does not work with arrays and adds a semicolon to the end of the class name for all arrays. This can be observed in the test case provided in the report where `ClassUtils.getShortClassName(sArray, null)` returns "String;".

Looking at the code snippet of the `getShortClassName` method, it seems that it calls `object.getClass()` to get the class of the object and returns the short name of the class. This behavior is consistent with the reported issue of adding a semicolon to the end of the class name for arrays.

To diagnose the issue:
1. The root cause of the problem is likely in the `getShortClassName` method where handling of array types needs to be adjusted to return the correct short class name without adding a semicolon.
2. The `getShortClassName` method should be modified to handle array types correctly and return the short class name without any additional characters.

Next, I will suggest the method that needs to be fixed.
